checks: At each row witness, all other inequalities stay strict on a sufficiently small neighborhood. Moving in the direction of the nonzero row normal proves irredundancy, and the relative neighborhood on the row hyperplane proves relative-interior facet contact. This gives exactly 2^n facets and verifies the witness theorem's hypotheses with A as the convex domain.

Parity completeness gives one integral midpoint partner in every class. Solving R(z)=y separately in each class gives exactly one integer 2y−p_r of that class; convexity gives preservation of P for a start in A.

Even outside A the orbit stays in conv({z}∪W), a compact set with finitely many lattice points. Midpoint convexity contracts distance to W by 1/2 at each step, so no orbit can stay at positive distance; W∩Z^n consists of fixed witnesses. No affine-rank premise on W is used.

Induction on the recurrence gives z−p_s=Σ_j 2^j(p_s−p_[z_j]), including the empty root path. Every term has nonnegative a_s-margin, and a nonroot requires at least one distinct digit, which gives strict exposure and excludes it from L.

On P the potential has the claimed zero set. Taking a maximum of the rowwise half-contractions is legitimate. If nonroots exist, their least positive value δ exists by finiteness; with k=1+ceil(log₂(V/δ)), V/2^k≤δ/2. If P consists only of roots the logarithmic estimate is vacuous.
